args.message:
Fix round_money to use ROUND_HALF_EVEN per FIN-212

The docstring claimed banker's rounding per FIN-212, but the
implementation used ROUND_HALF_UP, causing the nightly build to
fail (tests expect 2.675 -> 2.68 but 2.665 -> 2.66).

args.head: fix/FIN-212-bankers-rounding
args.title: Fix banker's rounding in round_money (FIN-212)
args.body:
## Summary
The nightly build failure in `tests/test_money.py` was caused by `round_money` in `src/money.py` using `ROUND_HALF_UP` while its docstring (and the spec FIN-212) calls for banker's rounding (`ROUND_HALF_EVEN`). This emits the wrong results for half-cent ties, e.g. `2.665` rounded to `2.67` instead of the expected `2.66`.

## Changes
- Switched the rounding mode to `ROUND_HALF_EVEN` in `round_money`, so ties at the half-cent round to the nearest even cent, per FIN-212.

## Verification
- CI passed on this branch (`tests/test_money.py` passes, including the banker's-rounding assertions).

Done. Here's a summary:

**Root cause:** `src/money.py`'s `round_money` claimed banker's rounding (per FIN-212) in its docstring but actually used `ROUND_HALF_UP`, so half-cent ties rounded incorrectly (e.g., 2.665 → 2.67 instead of 2.66), failing `tests/test_money.py` in the nightly build.

**Actions taken:**
1. Created branch `fix/FIN-212-bankers-rounding` from main.
2. Fixed the one-line bug: switched `ROUND_HALF_UP` → `ROUND_HALF_EVEN` in `src/money.py`.
3. Ran CI on the branch — it **passed** (run `ci-0001`).
4. Opened PR #101 against main requesting review from **alex**: https://git.example/payments-service/pull/101

Per policy, merging into main requires code-owner approval, so I have not merged — the PR is ready for alex's review.
